summary: Object.assign copies enumerable own properties from each source into a target object.
documentation: Object.assign copies enumerable own properties from each source into a target object. Later sources overwrite earlier values for a shared key. Using a new empty target keeps the original top-level objects unchanged, but the copy is shallow.
inputs: An array of plain JSON settings objects, with ordinary keys only.
returns: One object containing the merged settings.
caution: Nested objects are replaced rather than recursively merged. Do not use arbitrary untrusted property names for application configuration without a key allowlist.
scenarios: Combine documented defaults with per-page display settings.
Apply a sequence of approved report-format overrides.
Build a one-level options object for a reusable component.
title: Layer settings in order
problem: Input is an array of plain settings objects without special prototype-related keys. Merge them left to right into a new object. Later keys win; nested objects replace whole earlier nested objects.
goal: Use Object.assign() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Start with {} as the target and spread the sources.
